ZinCallingConvention.name: zincc
ZinCallingConvention.IntegerArgumentRegisters: rdi rsi rdx rcx r8 r9
ZinCallingConvention.FloatArgumentRegisters: xmm0 xmm1 xmm2 xmm3 xmm4 xmm5 xmm6 xmm7
ZinCallingConvention.VectorArgumentRegisters: xmm0-xmm7 for vectors of 128 bits or less when register-compatible
ZinCallingConvention.CallerSaved: rax rcx rdx rsi rdi r8 r9 r10 r11 xmm0-xmm15
ZinCallingConvention.CalleeSaved: rbx rbp r12 r13 r14 r15 rsp

ScalarClassification.Rule: Integer-like values of 1..64 bits use INTEGER class and are zero-extended for unsigned or sign-extended for signed register transport.
Integer-like values of 65..128 bits use two INTEGER eightbytes, low bits first.
Integer-like values above 128 bits use MEMORY class.
Pointers, optionals using pointer niches, enums <=64 bits and error tags <=64 bits use INTEGER class.
Vectors <=128 bits use SSE class; larger vectors use MEMORY unless a future target ABI version explicitly extends this rule.

AggregateClassification.Rule: Zero-sized values consume no register or stack slot.
Non-packed aggregates of size 1..16 bytes are partitioned into one or two consecutive eightbytes.
Each eightbyte is recursively classified INTEGER, SSE, or MEMORY from its contained fields.
Mixed INTEGER/SSE aggregates consume one register from the corresponding register bank per eightbyte, in source-layout order.
If any eightbyte is MEMORY, if required alignment exceeds 16, if size exceeds 16 bytes, or if register banks cannot satisfy the complete aggregate, the entire aggregate is passed in memory.
Packed aggregates are MEMORY unless their source type is explicitly bitcast to a scalar/vector.
Arrays are aggregates and follow the same recursive classification.
Tagged unions are classified from their concrete in-memory tag+payload layout. Untagged unions are classified from their maximum-size/max-alignment storage.

ArgumentAssignment.Rule: Source expressions evaluate left-to-right before ABI placement.
Classified register arguments consume registers from their class bank in declaration order.
A multi-eightbyte aggregate is assigned registers atomically; if all required registers are unavailable, the entire aggregate goes to stack memory.
Stack arguments use naturally aligned slots of at least 8 bytes. Final pre-call rsp alignment is 16 bytes.
A hidden large-return pointer, when present, consumes rdi before user integer arguments.

NormalReturn.Rule: Register-compatible values <=16 bytes use the same two-eightbyte classifier as arguments.
All larger/MEMORY returns use caller-provided return storage; the hidden pointer is passed as the first integer argument and returned unchanged in rax.

MultipleReturn.Rule: A source tuple/multiple return is classified exactly as its concrete tuple layout.
If register-compatible and <=16 bytes it uses the normal aggregate return registers.
Otherwise it uses caller-provided return storage.

ErrorUnionReturn.Rule: The error tag always occupies rax and therefore payload classification uses the dedicated payload bank below rather than the normal-return rax slot.
A payload whose flattened ABI representation fits at most four INTEGER and four SSE payload registers is returned there in layout order.
A larger/MEMORY payload uses caller-provided payload storage passed as the first integer argument. rax still returns the error tag.
Payload registers/storage are undefined on failure unless the source-level error type explicitly documents otherwise.

ZinCallingConvention.StackArguments: Arguments not assigned registers are laid out in call-frame order with required alignment; physical placement may be right-to-left but source evaluation remains left-to-right.
ZinCallingConvention.TailCalls: Permitted only when calling convention, hidden-return requirements, stack layout, cleanup stack, and return representation are compatible.
ZinCallingConvention.VarArgs: zincc has no untyped varargs in 1.0. Foreign C varargs use the selected foreign ABI rules.
